newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian queen returns as political crisis eases.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian queen returns as political crisis eases.

text.p: Queen Norodom Monineath returned to Cambodia on Thursday to a warm welcome as a crisis over the country's monarchy appeared to ease.

The queen, who had accompanied King Norodom Sihanouk to Beijing for his medical treatment, received a bipartisan greeting by co-Premier Prince Norodom Ranariddh and Bun Rany, the wife of co-Premier Hun Sen.

Questions over the monarchy's future role sparked a bitter political feud between the co-premiers that many viewed as the most serious threat yet to the fragile coalition Ranariddh and Hun Sen formed after the 1993 U.N.-sponsored elections.
But the bipartisan welcome sent a signal that the leadership had survived the row, diplomats and Cambodian analysts said.
"This shows support for the monarchy from both sides," said one diplomat.
Sihanouk remains in Beijing for treatment following eye surgery.
Reacting to Sihanouk's comment last month that he was considering abdication, Hun Sen had warned that elections would be cancelled if the king stepped down to enter politics.
He also said he would ask Sihanouk to ban royal family members from politics unless they renounced their royal status.
Ranariddh and his royalist FUNCINPEC party vowed to support Sihanouk were he to enter politics and defended their right to hold office.
After days of verbal attacks, the two leaders unexpectedly appeared to have resolved the issue. On Wednesday, both parties agreed to set national elections for November 1998.

Several analysts said they believed moderates in Hun Sen's Cambodian People's Party (CPP) had convinced him to ease his attacks on the monarchy and extend an olive branch by pushing for democratic polls next year.
The warm welcome for Queen Monineath was a continuing sign of good will from the CPP, they said, noting the presence of CPP President Chea Sim at the airport.
